findings.title: Denial as covering visible signs and their care demand
findings.claim: The focus denial can also be heard as covering visible signs together with the concrete care they make perceptible.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries physical covering and sign-directed denial, while the visible-sign carrier meets the supplied feeding-and-need context; their contact changes denial from a bare mental refusal into an active covering of an evident demand.
findings.reader_payoff: The sign-denial verdict acquires a practical ethical edge: what is covered is something that can be seen and answered.
findings.containment: This is a focus-bound activated coloring of the ordinary sign-denial reading; it does not make every root use physical concealment or claim that all care obligations are linguistically encoded in the focus.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding supplies the focus relation, while the care contact is corroborated by legacy HFT evidence whose context morphology is not supplied.
